title: The check-in never says which key to press, and the same key means opposite things morning and evening
method: end-to-end render of the composer check-ins `cura run` speaks, cross-read against CuraResponder.handle_dtmf and CuraVoice._build_twiml
triggers: press 1 in the morning after 'Have you had breakfast?'
press 2 in the evening after 'Do you have grab bars in your bathroom?'

must_not_contain: opposite things at different times of day

observed_at_discovery: cura/__main__.py _run_scheduled speaks CheckinComposer output and places the call with gather_response=True, so a digit is collected. Rendered for a two-medication profile, neither the morning nor the evening check-in contains the word 'press' anywhere -- the morning ends 'Have you had breakfast? Even something small gives you energy for the day.' and the evening ends on a home-safety question. CuraResponder.handle_dtmf then reads digit 1 as medication_confirmed in 'checkin' context and as help_requested in 'evening' context, and digit 2 as help_requested in 'checkin' and all_good in 'evening'. So a yes to 'have you had breakfast' is filed as a medication confirmation (and reaches the caregiver as 'Meds: all confirmed'), and a no at night is filed as all_good. Separately, the Gather built by CuraVoice._build_twiml carries no action attribute, so the digit is not posted to /voice/checkin-response at all -- status_callback is a call-lifecycle URL, not the Gather action. Repro exit 1, 3 failed.
